We're 90 minutes from billing run start. Pipeline deadlock, primary analytics cluster is frozen.

Option A: failover to read replica. Billing runs on time. 15-minute data gap, manual reconciliation needed.

Option B: hold, fix the lock in place. Billing delayed 2-3 hours. No gap, but we miss SLA window.

I need neutral risk modeling on both. Reconciliation complexity vs SLA penalty exposure. Do not recommend. Just the numbers and trade-offs clean.

No SLA schedule, gap volume, or reconciliation-hour estimate was provided. Only the times you stated can be treated as inputs. Dollar exposure cannot be computed from this.

**Stated inputs**

| | A: failover to replica | B: hold, fix lock |
|---|---|---|
| Billing start | On schedule | +2–3 h |
| Data completeness | 15 min gap (your figure) | No gap (your figure) |
| SLA window | Met | Missed |
| Follow-on work | Manual reconciliation | Delay handling only |

Clock: 90 min to run start.

**A — reconciliation complexity (not a dollar figure)**

Drivers, all unknown here:

- Event count and billed value in that 15 min (call it \(G\)).
- Whether the gap is missing events, late events, or both.
- Whether invoices go out before recon (corrections vs prevent).
- Idempotency: credit-memo / rebill / void rate.
- Staff hours and error rate on \(G\).

Cost shape: \(C_A \approx\) (labor on \(G\)) + (expected misbill on \(G\)) + (dispute/chargeback on issued invoices). Linear in \(G\) if invoices are held; jumps if invoices are sent first.

Unverified in your description: replica freshness. A frozen primary can mean lag **>** 15 min. If lag is larger, \(G\) is larger than stated.

**B — SLA penalty exposure (not a dollar figure)**

Drivers, all unknown here:

- Penalty function \(P\): flat per incident, per hour, % of invoice, per customer, cap, grace.
- Whether 2 h and 3 h are the same breach tier.
- Notice/cure terms; whether a delay notice reduces \(P\).
- Downstream cutoffs (ACH/card windows) that turn a 2–3 h miss into a next-day miss.

Cost shape: \(C_B = P(2\text{–}3\text{ h})\) + any missed payment-window cost. Independent of \(G\) unless the contract ties credits to billed volume.

**Trade-off (structural)**

- A trades a **bounded time gap** (15 min of data, plus whatever extra replica lag exists) for **on-time SLA**. Residual is operational and customer-correction risk on \(G\), after money may already have been billed.
- B trades a **2–3 h schedule miss** for **complete data**. Residual is contractual \(P\) and any payment-cutoff slip. No gap-recon on billing contents, as you stated.

Which is larger is \(C_A(G)\) vs \(C_B(P)\). That inequality is not determined by the times alone.

**Not in the model (would change the numbers)**

SLA clause and cap; \(G\) in events and currency; whether A bills then corrects or holds invoices; measured replica lag now; whether the deadlock is on the billing write path or analytics only.

One figure that would let this be numeric: the SLA penalty formula and the billed value (or event count) in a typical 15 min.
I need the sla penalty formula and the billing value per 15 min window. Also current replica lag in seconds. Do you have that from the telemetry or do I need to pull it.

I do not have telemetry, the SLA contract, or billing volumes. Those are not in this conversation and I cannot query your systems.

You need to pull:

1. **SLA penalty formula** — contract: flat vs per-hour vs % of invoice, grace, cap, notice/cure.
2. **Billed value (or event count) in a typical 15 min window** — and, if possible, the same for the current window.
3. **Replica lag now** — seconds (and whether it is growing). A frozen primary can make lag larger than 15 min.

Until those three are in hand, \(C_A\) and \(C_B\) stay unquantified.

SLA penalty is 5% of quarterly billing per hour past 7pm, cap at 15%. Billing value per 15 min window is roughly $40k. Replica lag is 22 seconds and stable.

That enough to quantify.

Those three inputs bound **A**. They do not produce a dollar figure for **B** without quarterly billing \(Q\) (the base the 5% applies to) and without clock time vs 7pm.

**A — gap (your figures)**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Stated gap | 15 min |
| Value in a 15 min window | ~$40k |
| Replica lag | 22 s, stable |
| Prorated lag | \(40{,}000 \times 22/900 \approx \$980\) |

Treat billed value in the hole as **~$40k** if the 15 min is real missing data, or **~$1k** if the only missing data is the 22 s lag. Those two figures are not the same hole: 22 s lag does not explain a 15 min gap. Failover/cutover time would.

\(C_A\) is **not** $40k lost. It is labor to recon that window plus expected misbill/dispute on a **fraction** of ~$40k (or ~$1k). Upper bound on wrong billed amount from the gap is on the order of that window, not a 5–15% revenue event.

**B — SLA (your formula)**

Penalty \(= \min(0.05 \times h \times Q,\ 0.15Q)\)  
\(h\) = hours **past 7pm** (partial-hour rule not given: ceil vs prorate changes \(h\)).

| \(h\) past 7pm | Penalty |
|---|---|
| 1 | \(0.05Q\) |
| 2 | \(0.10Q\) |
| 3+ | \(0.15Q\) (cap) |

A **2–3 h delay** is **\(0.10Q\)–\(0.15Q\)** only if that delay is 2–3 hours **after 7pm**. “Miss SLA” only tells you \(h \ge 1\). Run start is in 90 min; wall clock vs 7pm was not given.

**Scale (still not a recommendation)**

A is \(O(\$10^4)\) of **window value**, with expected cash cost a fraction of that.  
B is **5–15% of \(Q\)**.

Break-even if you counted the **entire** ~$40k window as lost (an upper bound on A, not the expected cost):

- vs 2 h past 7pm: \(0.10Q = \$40\text{k} \Rightarrow Q = \$400\text{k}\)
- vs 3 h past 7pm: \(0.15Q = \$40\text{k} \Rightarrow Q \approx \$267\text{k}\)

If \(Q\) is above that range, even worst-case A is smaller than B’s contract hit. Expected A is lower than $40k, which moves the break-even \(Q\) down.

**Still missing for dollars on B**

1. \(Q\) in the SLA clause (company-wide vs the billed accounts).  
2. Whether the 2–3 h slip is 2–3 h past **7pm**.
Q is ~$4m for the billing run. Clock is 6:10pm. So 2 hour delay means first hour past 7pm, 3 hour delay means 2 hours past. That caps at 0.10Q or 0.15Q.

Those inputs fix the **dollar scale**. They do not fix **how many hours past 7pm** apply. Two clock stories in this thread disagree, and that changes \(B\) by hundreds of thousands of dollars.

**Contract arithmetic** (your formula, \(Q \approx \$4{,}000{,}000\))

| Hours past 7pm (\(h\)) | Penalty \(\min(0.05 h Q,\ 0.15Q)\) |
|---|---|
| 1 | **$200,000** |
| 2 | **$400,000** |
| 3+ | **$600,000** (cap) |

Partial-hour rule still unknown (floor / prorate / ceil). Ceil on 40–70 min past 7pm is a full extra $200k.

Your last mapping (2 h delay \(\rightarrow\) \(h=1\), 3 h delay \(\rightarrow\) \(h=2\)) is **$200k–$400k**, not 0.10Q–0.15Q. 0.10Q is two hours past 7pm; 0.15Q is the cap at three.

**A — gap (unchanged order of magnitude)**

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Stated 15 min window | ~$40,000 billed value |
| 22 s replica lag | ~$980 |
| Expected cash cost | recon labor + a **fraction** of that window (misbill/dispute), not $40k lost |

22 s lag still does not equal a 15 min hole. Cutover time would.

**Clock conflict (this is what sets \(h\))**

Stated together: now **6:10pm**, **90 min to run start** \(\Rightarrow\) scheduled start **7:40pm**, SLA clock **7:00pm**.

| Path | When billing runs | \(h\) past 7pm | \(C_B\) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Your mapping (2–3 h delay = 1–2 h past 7pm) | ~8:00–9:00pm | 1–2 | $200k–$400k |
| 7:40 start + 2–3 h delay | 9:40–10:40pm | ~2.7–3.7 \(\rightarrow\) cap if ceil/3+ | **$400k–$600k** |
| A “on time” at 7:40 | 7:40pm | 40 min | $0, ~$80k prorate, or **$200k** if any hour past 7pm bills a full hour |

If A is truly inside the SLA, scheduled start cannot be 7:40pm under a 7pm cutoff unless the penalty is on **finish** time and the run is short enough to finish by 7pm, or “90 min to start” is wrong.

**Trade-off (numbers only)**

- \(C_A\): four-digit to low five-digit, bounded by a ~$40k window.
- \(C_B\): **$200k, $400k, or $600k** depending on \(h\), which is not identified until start/finish vs 7pm is identified.
- Even treating the entire $40k window as lost, \(C_A \ll C_B\) at every positive \(h\).

**Still open (changes \(B\), not the inequality vs $40k)**

1. Actual start and finish timestamps vs 7:00pm, and whether partial hours ceil.  
2. Whether contract “quarterly billing” is this ~$4m run or a different trailing-quarter figure (scale \(C_B\) linearly if it is not $4m).

ok. I also need to factor contract breach penalties beyond the sla. Some of our contracts have a 25% quarterly credit clause if billing is late. That's separate from the sla cap. And it applies per customer. Not all customers have it but the largest three do.

The 25% clause is not a dollar figure until the three customers’ quarterly bases are known. On the facts given it attaches to **B** (late), not **A** (on-time run). It stacks on the SLA; it does not replace the cap.

**New term (your clause)**

\[
C_{25}=0.25\,(Q_1+Q_2+Q_3)
\]

per late event, those three customers only. Unknown: each \(Q_i\), and whether “late” is any miss of 7pm, miss of the SLA window, or delay of 2–3 h. Unknown: whether a credit is one quarter only or repeats.

**B — stacked exposure**

SLA (from prior inputs, \(Q\approx\$4\text{m}\)) plus \(C_{25}\):

| \(h\) past 7pm | SLA | + 25% credits | Total \(C_B\) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | $200,000 | \(0.25\sum Q_i\) | $200,000 + \(C_{25}\) |
| 2 | $400,000 | \(0.25\sum Q_i\) | $400,000 + \(C_{25}\) |
| 3+ | $600,000 | \(0.25\sum Q_i\) | $600,000 + \(C_{25}\) |

Clock still disagrees with itself: 6:10pm + 90 min to start \(\Rightarrow\) 7:40 start; a 2–3 h hold is then ~9:40–10:40pm (\(h\approx 2.7\)–\(3.7\), SLA **$400k–$600k** if hours ceil at 3). Your mapping (2 h delay \(\rightarrow h=1\), 3 h \(\rightarrow h=2\)) is **$200k–$400k** SLA. Partial-hour rule still unknown.

**A — unchanged class of cost**

On-time start \(\Rightarrow\) 25% late credits **do not fire** on the stated trigger. Residual is recon + a fraction of the ~$40k / ~$1k window (15 min stated gap vs 22 s lag). No contract % of \(Q\) or of \(\sum Q_i\) is in the inputs for A.

Wrong or gapped invoices could be a **different** clause (accuracy, not lateness). That was not provided; it is not included in either column.

**Scale (still not a recommendation)**

- \(C_A\): four-digit to low five-digit, bounded by ~$40k of window value.
- \(C_B\): $200k–$600k SLA **plus** \(0.25\sum Q_i\).

Break-even of \(C_{25}\) alone vs the entire $40k window: \(\sum Q_i=\$160\text{k}\). If the three customers’ combined quarterly is above that, the late-credit term by itself exceeds worst-case A. SLA is additional.

**Not in the model**

\(Q_1,Q_2,Q_3\) (or their share of the $4m run); exact “late” definition vs 7:00pm; start/finish timestamps and ceil vs prorate; whether A’s gap triggers an accuracy credit.

The figure that prices the new term is the sum of quarterly billing for those three customers.
